title: Control-plane managed owner-mapping config (versioned + audited) for incident taxonomy
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Reliability Program: Incident taxonomy + ownership mapping
summary: Create a control-plane-managed ownership mapping config for incident taxonomy (type/subtype -> primary owner, secondary/consulted, escalation channel, runbook links). Config must be versioned, reviewed, auditable, and safely rolled out/rolled back. This mapping is used by incident-bot and alert/paging routing to reduce ambiguity and improve MTTR.
body:
Context
- Incident taxonomy v1 requires incident_type/subtype classification and an accountable owner. Today we have multiple copies of an owner map (spreadsheets / bot code / routing rules), which creates drift during incidents.
- Goal is to centralize the mapping in the control plane so it can be: (1) changed quickly during operational shifts, (2) validated and reviewed, (3) audited, and (4) rolled out safely.

Problem statement
- On-call needs a single source of truth: given incident_type/subtype, resolve a primary owner team + escalation channel + runbook(s).
- Changes must be attributable (who/when/why), and reversible without redeploying the bot or routing stack.

Requirements
1) Source of truth in control plane
- Store an "incident owner mapping" configuration in the control plane.
- Must support: incident_type, subtype, primary_owner_team, secondary_teams, consulted_teams, escalation_slack_channel, runbook_urls, notes.
- Must support an explicit "unknown/unclassified" entry to route to SRE as default.

2) Versioning + change review
- Every change creates a new immutable version (e.g., monotonically increasing integer or semver-like string).
- Change must include: change_reason, requested_by, related_ticket (Linear key), and optional incident link.
- Maintain a readable change log (human-friendly diff summary) and a machine-readable audit trail.

3) Audit logging
- Emit audit logs on: create version, promote to active, rollback, and access (read) from production services.
- Audit fields: actor, auth method, request ID, previous version, new version, diff summary, timestamp.

4) Safe rollout + rollback
- Promote new versions via a staged rollout mechanism:
  - Stage 0: created (not active)
  - Stage 1: canary active (optional allowlist by workspace/service or percentage)
  - Stage 2: globally active
- Rollback must be a single action in the control plane to set active_version back to last known good.
- Services must cache last-known-good mapping and continue operating if control plane is degraded.

5) Validation + guardrails
- Validate incident_type/subtype are in the v1 allowlist (to prevent cardinality explosion + typos).
- Validate owner team slugs are from a known set (SRE, Platform-Control-Plane, Smart-Routing, Infra-Fleet, Observability, Serving-Runtime, Security-Ops, Private-Deployments).
- Enforce maximum list sizes (e.g., secondary/consulted <= 3) and URL allowlist for runbooks (Confluence domains).

Proposed design (implemented)
- Control plane adds a new config object: IncidentOwnerMappingConfig.
- Endpoints (internal):
  - GET /internal/config/incident-owner-mapping (returns active version + payload + ETag)
  - GET /internal/config/incident-owner-mapping/versions (list + change log)
  - POST /internal/config/incident-owner-mapping (create new version; RBAC protected)
  - POST /internal/config/incident-owner-mapping/promote (set active version; RBAC protected)
  - POST /internal/config/incident-owner-mapping/rollback (set active version back; RBAC protected)
- Storage:
  - Versioned blobs + metadata stored in control plane config store.
  - Audit events sent to audit-log pipeline.

Consumers
- incident-bot: resolve owner + escalation channel when incident_type/subtype is set or suggested.
- paging router: use resolved primary owner for paging when type is known, otherwise fall back to existing routing.
- (future) Console ops views: display resolved owner + mapping version for transparency.

Operational notes
- Default owner for unclassified/unknown is SRE.
- During live incidents, if mapping is wrong, SRE can hotfix mapping via control plane (with review path below), without code deploy.

Review & approvals
- Required approvers for promote-to-global:
  - Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park)
  - SRE program lead (Rafael Mendes)
- Recommended reviewers for changes affecting labels/routing behavior:
  - Observability standards (Allison Grant)
  - Routing ownership (Mina Haddad)

Out of scope
- Building a full UI in Console for editing (this ticket provides APIs + audit + guardrails; UI tracked elsewhere).
- Deep incident classification logic or auto-suggestion heuristics (incident-bot ticket/PR handles heuristics).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Control plane stores owner mapping as versioned config and exposes read API for consumers.
2) Create/promote/rollback operations are RBAC protected and generate audit log events.
3) Validation prevents unknown incident_type/subtype and unknown owner team slugs from being promoted to active.
4) Staged rollout supported (at minimum: created -> active; optional canary), with a documented rollback procedure.
5) incident-bot can resolve owner via control-plane mapping in staging environment (end-to-end smoke test).
6) Change log is accessible (versions endpoint or equivalent) and includes actor + reason + ticket link.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging):
- Deploy control plane changes behind feature flag: incident_owner_mapping_config_enabled.
- Seed initial mapping from v1 taxonomy table (SRE-provided JSON).
- Validate incident-bot in staging can fetch and resolve owner for top 10 incident types.

Phase 2 (prod canary):
- Enable read path in prod for a limited set of internal workspaces/services (incident-bot only).
- Monitor: control plane QPS, error rates, p95 latency, cache hit rate.

Phase 3 (prod global):
- Promote mapping version to global active.
- Enable paging router read path (if ready) or keep as read-only until ENG-4823 is complete.

Comms:
- Announce "mapping is now source of truth" in #eng-sre and #eng-platform.
- Link to change process and approvers.
rollback_plan:
If incorrect routing/owner resolution is observed:
1) Use control plane rollback action to set active_version to last known good.
2) Verify incident-bot is resolving owner against rolled-back version (check bot debug output includes mapping version).
3) Post in incident channel + #eng-sre with the rollback version and reason.
4) Open follow-up task to correct mapping and re-promote with required approvals.

If control plane is degraded:
- Consumers continue using last-known-good cached mapping and fall back to SRE for unknown/unclassified; no paging hard-fail.
audit_and_compliance:
Audit events emitted for: create version, promote, rollback, read-access (sampled) in prod.
Audit fields include: actor, team, RBAC role, request_id, previous_version, new_version, diff_summary, related_ticket, timestamp.
RBAC: only Platform Control Plane on-call + SRE program lead group can promote/rollback; broader group can create draft versions (created stage) but cannot promote without approvals.
Retention: align with existing control plane audit log retention policy (per Security Ops guidance).

comments: 2025-12-11 (Ethan Park): Drafted schema based on Drive proposal. Added strict allowlist validation for incident_type/subtype to avoid metric label drift and typo-driven new categories. Will treat taxonomy list as static for v1; updates require synchronized change with SRE taxonomy owners.

2025-12-13 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on allowlist. Please add explicit 'unknown/unclassified' mapping that resolves to SRE with #incidents escalation channel so we have a safe default when on-call can't decide quickly.

2025-12-16 (Allison Grant): Observability request: include mapping_version in debug logs from consumers. Not a metric label (cardinality), but we should be able to answer “which version was used” during postmortems.

2025-12-18 (Fiona McCarthy): Security review note: promote/rollback endpoints must require strong auth + RBAC; audit log must include actor identity and source IP/service identity. Sampling read-access audit logs in prod is fine; full logging may be noisy.

2026-01-06 (Ethan Park): Implemented create/promote/rollback with immutable versions. Added diff summary generation (best-effort) for change log; stored change_reason + related_ticket. Consumers receive active_version + payload + ETag.

2026-01-10 (Dylan Brooks): incident-bot integration plan: bot will fetch mapping at startup + refresh every 60s with ETag; if fetch fails, use cached mapping and show warning in /incident debug. This supports control plane outages without blocking incident ops.

2026-01-15 (Rafael Mendes): Requested staged rollout: start with incident-bot only, then enable paging router later. Please document how to do a rollback during an active incident (single command / API call).

2026-01-22 (Ethan Park): PR ready for review. Added 'created' vs 'active' states; canary flag is implemented as service-allowlist (incident-bot only) for now. True percentage rollout deferred unless we see need.
2026-01-26 (Ethan Park): Merged and deployed to staging; seeded v1 mapping; ran smoke tests for 15 top incident categories. Preparing prod canary with incident-bot only.

2026-01-28 (Rafael Mendes): Marking done. Verified prod incident-bot resolves owner and prints mapping_version. Rollback procedure documented in runbook. Follow-up: Console UI for editing mapping tracked separately.
